thread.title: Students welcome new look at renovated Bedford High - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Students welcome new look at renovated Bedford High - NewsBreak

author: Vincent Picone
title: Students welcome new look at renovated Bedford High - NewsBreak
text:
By Vincent Picone ,
6 hours ago
BEDFORD, Pa. (WTAJ) — Students returning to Bedford High School this year are seeing a very different building than the one they left behind last spring.
A roughly $51 million renovation has transformed much of the school’s interior, giving students updated classrooms, new flooring and lighting, new sports fields, a redesigned cafeteria and future plans for the exterior of the building.
The changes were noticeable right away for Senior Mackenzie Clapper, who said improvements that may seem small have made a major difference.
“Simply the flooring and the lighting. It's like, such a big difference.”
School officials say the previous major renovation took place about 30 years ago. The latest project represents a much larger investment in the school and its facilities.
Among the changes getting the most attention from students is the cafeteria.
Clapper said the updated space gives Bedford High School a completely different atmosphere.
“I feel like I'm like older now instead of, like, the long tables with the no back chairs.”
Junior Grey Livengood said students had been looking forward to seeing the new cafeteria and were surprised by how different it looked once they returned.
“It looks a lot better than where we were at last year,” Livengood said. “I knew it was going to look nicer than the old cafeteria, but I was not expecting this.”
The project is not finished yet.
Construction crews still have exterior work to complete, along with additional lighting and work on the gym. The overall project is currently about 90% complete.
Despite the remaining work, students say the improvements have already changed the feel of the school.
For some, the updated facilities are more than just cosmetic changes. Having a newer and more welcoming environment can give students another reason to be excited about coming to school.
The district will celebrate the progress with a ribbon-cutting ceremony Saturday, Aug. 22 as the renovation reaches the 90% completion mark.
